title: Label Ambiguity Decision Tree — scratch
content:
Purpose
This is a personal scratchpad to capture a compact decision tree for labelers when they hit ambiguous examples during the cleanup pass. Goal: reduce inter-annotator variance for tricky spans and create a short checklist that can be turned into UI tooltips.

Notes to self (high-level)
- Keep decisions conservative: prefer fewer, higher-precision labels over over-tagging.
- Capture explicit fallback: when in doubt, mark as "ambiguous" + freeform note. We'll sample ambiguous pool for adjudication.
- Add explicit rules for tokenization mismatches (IDs, punctuation, unicode).

Decision flow (first pass)
1) Is there a clear label from the schema?
   - YES -> apply label. Add confidence tag: high.
   - NO -> go to 2
2) Is the entity an identifier (serial, order id, uuid, url param)?
   - If pattern matches (regex heuristics): LABEL = ID; unless product label expects NATURAL_LANGUAGE.
   - If ID is embedded in natural language phrase (e.g., "order #12345 was late") prefer span that excludes "#" unless schema expects punctuation.
3) Overlapping spans (person vs org vs title)
   - If span contains honorifics/titles (Dr., Prof., CEO) and a person name -> label = PERSON; add derived attribute = title (optional).
   - If company name appears with role ("Acme Corp CEO John Doe") -> two spans: ORG = "Acme Corp", PERSON = "John Doe". If UI disallows overlapping spans, choose split that preserves named entity boundaries (ORG leftmost; PERSON rightmost).
4) Nested concepts (product names that are also company names)
   - If occurrence is in marketing copy ("Acme's new RocketPhone") -> PRODUCT. If in formal legal text ("Acme, Inc.") -> ORG. Fall back: look at adjacent verbs ("released" -> PRODUCT).
5) Dates & relative times
   - Exact dates (YYYY-MM-DD, Month Day, Year) -> DATE.
   - Relative terms (next week, tomorrow) -> NATURAL_DATE if schema includes. Otherwise annotate as CONTEXT
6) Toxic / violent content that triggers safety labels
   - If text contains threats or explicit slurs: tag SAFETY and add freeform note for severity. Don't attempt to classify sentiment at same time unless asked.

Tokenization gotchas
- Emojis attached to words: treat emoji as separate token span if it carries meaning (e.g., "great 😅" -> sentiment token separate).
- URLs with path fragments: if label is URL, capture full path excluding tracking params (?utm_...). Add note to strip params in downstream.
- Hyphenated names: treat as single span ("Anne-Marie") unless hyphen indicates subtraction (context).

Examples (explicit cases)
1) Input: "Reached out to support@acme.com and they replied."
   Labels: EMAIL = "support@acme.com". Note: "they" is pronoun — do NOT label pronouns as PERSON.
2) Input: "Order 0x4f3a failed at 2024-09-15."
   Labels: ID = "0x4f3a"; DATE = "2024-09-15". If sequence looks hex, mark as HEX_ID tag in metadata.
3) Input: "President-elect Jane Q. Public spoke today."
   Labels: PERSON = "Jane Q. Public". Role/title "President-elect" -> optional ROLE tag if supported.
4) Input: "We launched Acme RocketPhone (v2) in June."
   Labels: PRODUCT = "Acme RocketPhone (v2)"; DATE = "June" (ambiguous year -> NATURAL_DATE with low confidence).
5) Input: "Click here: https://example.com/path?utm_source=campaign&id=789"
   Labels: URL = "https://example.com/path?id=789" (strip utm params). Note: keep query params that look like identifiers.

Ambiguity heuristics (quick rules)
- Prefer human-readable forms: if one span reads naturally as a name, prefer PERSON.
- If both ORG and PRODUCT plausible, check capitalization patterns and presence of legal tokens (Inc, LLC) -> ORG.
- For single-word ambiguous tokens ("Mercury", "Saturn"), derive from surrounding verbs: "drove Mercury" -> CAR (if schema has PRODUCT/CAR), "studied Mercury" -> PLANET/ASTRO. If still unclear -> AMBIGUOUS.

QA sampling strategy
- Sample 2% of all labels where annotator confidence != high. Prioritize AMBIGUOUS and ID categories.
- Adjudicate ambiguous pool weekly; update quick heuristics doc.
- Track per-annotator disagreement heatmap; use small adjudication batches to calibrate.

UI tooltip copy (drafts)
- "Ambiguous? Mark as AMBIGUOUS and leave a short note. We'll review these weekly."
- "IDs: capture the core identifier; omit tracking params."
- "Overlapping names: prefer separate spans for company vs person; if UI blocks overlap, split into two adjacent spans."

Open questions (to resolve with Ravi / product)
- Do we want an explicit "ROLE" field when titles appear, or rely on freeform?
- How should the annotator UI display overlapping ORG+PERSON when underlying model expects single-span labels? Add a boolean "allow_overlap" in exporter?
- Should emoji ever be labeled as ENTITITES or only affect sentiment downstream?

Next steps (TODO)
- Draft a 1-page cheat sheet for new contractors (convert this doc).
- Add regex list for ID heuristics to repo (github link above).
- Create Jira ticket for ambiguous adjudication cadence and assign owner.

Random scratch bits
- Consider a tiny ML feature: heuristics-derived hint that suggests label with low confidence and asks annotator to confirm (speed up labeling).
- Metric idea: reduce ambiguous rate < 3% within 3 sprints.

End of scratchpad.

(If I reopen this in a week, merge repeated heuristics into Confluence page and strip personal notes.)
